# Gengchou v2.5.1

v2.5.1 is a fix release. Its centrepiece is that informational tray balloons
have never been displayed since v2.4.1: every notification Gengchou raised to
report something that already happened was accepted by Windows and then
silently dropped. Quota window reset reminders are the visible casualty. The
executable, settings, cache, and update identities are unchanged.

## Changes

- Fix a profile whose only usable provider is Grok never polling at all. The
  check that decides whether to start a poll read only the first three
  providers, so a setup showing and authorising Grok alone was treated as
  having nothing to poll and skipped every pass. A fresh install that detects
  Grok and nothing else lands exactly there. Affected since v2.5.0, where Grok
  was introduced.
- Fix every informational tray balloon. Gengchou destroyed the balloon's image
  handle as soon as `Shell_NotifyIcon` returned. That is correct for a tray
  icon's own image, which the shell copies during the call, but Windows 10 and
  11 render a tray balloon as a toast *after* the call returns, so the handle
  was already gone and nothing was drawn - while the call still reported
  success. Affected since v2.4.1: **quota window reset reminders**, the
  notification for a newly detected provider, and the one for a finished
  Claude CLI update. Warnings that require action, such as a rejected
  credential, were never affected.
- Fix the periodic provider detection sweep, which had never run. Its timer was
  armed on the taskbar-embedded widget window, whose window procedure has no
  branch for it, so every `WM_TIMER` was discarded. Also affected since v2.4.1.
  A provider installed and signed into after Gengchou's first run was therefore
  never announced.
- Run one detection sweep at startup on an existing installation, instead of
  waiting a full 30-minute interval for the first one. An upgrade that adds a
  provider now tells you about it while you are still there to notice, and
  quitting sooner than the interval no longer defers it again. Each provider is
  still announced at most once, ever.
- Notify about a provider that is not currently shown. Such a provider has no
  tray icon by definition, and per-provider icon mode removes the application
  icon as well, so the balloon had nowhere to attach. It now falls through to
  whichever icon the tray actually has, and a delivery that fails outright is
  written to the diagnostic log rather than discarded.
- Show the application icon in the notification area when no provider has been
  granted credential access, instead of one arbitrarily chosen provider's mark.
  Your per-provider icon preference is not modified; the provider icons return
  as soon as any provider is authorised again.
- Show the Gengchou icon in the title bar of the credential access dialog.
- Stop the taskbar widget's hover tooltip from reappearing next to the detail
  popup after a click opens it.
